author Matt Stults
subject Engineering findings F2-F11: the sweep, and eight defects in the renderer
Two adversarial reviews. Design findings stay parked (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q-15);
everything here is a defect.

F2 GENERALISED — the sweep, not the instance. Shape: anything that shells out
and decides pass/fail purely from stdout matching. `test_schema.py`'s clingo
calls now go through one helper that reads the RETURN CODE too, pinned by a
fake-interpreter pair copied from `test_link.py` (the reference the review
names as correct): one test proves a clingo that never ran is a complaint with
no `error` text anywhere, its partner proves 0/10/20/30 stay silent so
`return ['x']` cannot pass.

  NEW, missed by both reviews: `paper_pipeline/cq_check.py` — stage 0's only
  mechanical check on the design's written-first answers — had the same shape
  in both runners. With a clingo-less interpreter CQ-4.a, CQ-5.a, CQ-5.b and
  CQ-6.c all reported `pass` with nothing executed: their expectations are
  written as ABSENCES, and an absence is what a dead process produces. Return
  code alone was not enough for `link.py`, whose exit 1 means both "found
  errors" and "died"; the second observable is that it always prints.
  Also swept and sound: `mutate_schema.py`, `model/test_model.py`,
  `test_link.py` — except its live-run acceptance case, which derived `leaked`
  by regex from stdout and now asserts `returncode == 0` first.

F4 quoted string constants are DATA. `substitute` had no string awareness, so
`p("political_content is bad")` was rewritten into prose — and a declared label
inside a string was glossed AWAY, blinding RB1, whose whole job is to see one.
F5 a gloss carrying `«` defeated the flat `_strip` and left prose in RB1's,
RB3's and RB4's scans — RB3 fired on a CORRECT rendering. Fixed at INSERTION
(the markers must stay unambiguous), and declared as a note, never silently.
F6 `_CONVERSE`/`_CMP` now pinned over all six operators in both guard
positions, plus a bijection guard. These were 3 of the reviewer's 4 survivors.
F7 `_layer` min->max: pinned with the first item that mixes the two layers.
F8 `KEYWORDS` made the layers disagree: layer 1 refused a gloss `_gloss_slot`
used, so RB1 fired on a module declaring `count/1` saying "no definition was
available" — which was false. `#` already excludes the directives; only `not`
was load-bearing.
F9 ontology arguments were dressed in gloss markers, which INVERTED RB1's
classification. They go through `substitute` now. On the corpus this removes
six RB1 findings on m0014 — not a weakened check: `violence_act` is a declared
concept and the renderer now emits its definition instead of its label, which
is Invariant 1 being satisfied.
F10 `_rb1` iterated a set with prefix-blind replacement. Longest-first.

F11 the repair-turn USER blocks were unpriced in code and test. The arithmetic
is left alone (verified >= the true worst case for 1..5). The estimate's
surplus is exactly T(T-1)/2 copies of (system+user) — the same coefficient the
error-log term carries — so it covers the logs iff a log fits in one
system+user block. That is now a NAMED budget (8,000 chars; largest ever
produced: 1,294), priced into the hand-priced floor, and CHECKED.

F3 `translate.py --self-test` exits 1 and pytest read green. The wrapper now
asserts `returncode == 0` (pins no count) and is `xfail(strict=True)` naming
Q-4, so the red is VISIBLE and flips to a hard failure the day Q-4 is decided.
`dryrun.txt` NOT regenerated. Stale numbers corrected in REVIEW_QUEUE.md and
Q-4 — and the review's own "44 guards" is now 46, having moved again when the
anonymous-variable guard was restored.

10/10 hand mutants killed, including all 4 the reviewer found surviving.
500 passed + 1 xfail. mutate_schema 46 killed, 0 SURVIVORS. link --self-test
19/19. schema.py untouched. No API call, no spend.

commit 5cf82a4fc94220c3d7ef2c93239e44bb945d02ef
ordinal 104
date 2026-08-08 00:21:26 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Q-18: stage 0 competency check is red -- and a correction, it is NOT quiet
cq_check.py reports 14 as declared, 2 unexpected, 2 blocked. CQ-6.a and CQ-6.b
fail against their written-first expectations. Pre-existing and outside the
stage 1-4 scope, recorded so it is not lost.

THE CORRECTION: a subagent reported the tool "exits 0 anyway, so stage 0's
competency check is red and quiet", and I nearly filed that as a defect. It is
false -- cq_check.py exits 1. Both of us measured through `cmd | tail`, where
$? reports tail's status, not the program's.

The general lesson outlives the finding: `cmd | tail` silently discards the exit
code, and this repo's entire discipline is that a check must not be able to look
like it passed. Two independent agents produced the same false claim from that
one habit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 21813f2544ee8b50a7a78ff15de1bdc45e79ec62
ordinal 105
date 2026-08-08 00:27:39 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject stage 4: build R3, the derivation layer — 8 of 18 covering-set situations
`STEP_stage4.md` §2.1 specifies three read-back layers. `readback.py` produced
R1 and R2, so no DERIVATION reached any seat: the seats judged items and rules,
never why a verdict followed. `readback_r3.py` is the third layer, as a separate
module — `readback.py`'s public surface is untouched.

The pipeline, per §2.1/§2.2: compose a `%!trace_rule` per rule MECHANICALLY from
`readback.render_items` (never the model's authored `read_back`, which §2.2
demotes to a second opinion), run xclingo per derived verdict atom, parse the
ascii tree, and replace every leaf with its R1 rendering.

MEASURED, on the six stored modules that reach R3: 8 of 18 covering-set
situations have a non-empty derivation. Printed with its denominator, per
DEBUGGING_TIPS §2, and the ten that derive nothing are stamped `no-derivation`
rather than dropped.

Two defects found on live material and pinned:

* `o`, the ontology ablation guard, surfaced as a LEAF of every ontology-backed
  derivation and was reported as `readback-ungloss` — a false stop on renderer
  scaffolding. The guard is removed from R3's program rather than exempted by
  name; exempting a hard-coded symbol is how a real missing gloss would later
  hide.
* A body-less `asserts` fact carries R3's own label AND the one
  `--auto-tracing=facts` adds; xclingo joins them with `;`, and reading the
  payload as one quoted sentence put `asserts(m0079,oblige,produce_response)` in
  front of a seat. Invariant 1's exact failure, emitted by the layer written to
  fix it.

Every empty result BLOCKS: missing xclingo, `_` anywhere in the link scope
(refused BY NAME — it takes the whole link set's explanation down and exits 0),
an unparseable or truncated stream, a line R3 cannot place, and a verdict stage 3
derives that xclingo roots no tree at. Three redundant xclingo detectors, each
with its own RED test after the first sweep showed the return-code and sentinel
arms surviving on the others' coverage (DEBUGGING_TIPS §8).

RECORDED DEPARTURE: §2.1 says `--output ascii-trees -n 0 0`. [RAN] that alone
yields a tree with NO leaves, which makes R3's defining requirement vacuous, so
`--auto-tracing=facts` is added — the flag §0 finding (3) itself used.

TDD: RED first (collection error, then 11 failures), 33 tests, mutation sweep
21/21 killed, 0 survivors. Suite 634 -> 667, no regressions. No API calls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 9d3c9a4404540b6e182fd19a46663cde598a1a98
ordinal 106
date 2026-08-08 00:32:16 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject R3: carry §2.3's layer stamp, and keep a missing GLOSS out of it
§2.3 requires every rendering to record the layer that produced it and the
layer-1 fraction to be printed even when zero; R3's nodes were dropping it, so
fluent English and glossed ASP were indistinguishable in the derivation.

⚠️ Written the other way round first, and the assertion was WRONG. An
unglossed leaf was stamped layer 1 on the reasoning that a bare term IS layer
1's fallback form. `readback._gloss_slot` already stamps the same marked hole
layer 2 inside a rule rendering, so R3 and R1 would have disagreed about one
missing definition — and it re-merges the two things §2.3 says must not be
blurred: a missing TEMPLATE is our gap and costs fluency, a missing GLOSS is a
hole in the translation and stops the clause. The stamp tracks templates; the
ERROR carries the gloss.

⚠️ The layer-1 fixture also had to change. `readback` has layer-2 templates
for aggregates, comparisons, intervals and conditional literals — [RAN] all
four render at layer 2 — so reaching for "something exotic" did not exercise
the fallback at all. Pooling (`p(X;Y)`) does.

Suite 667 -> 670. Mutation sweep re-run: 21/21 killed, 0 survivors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author Matt Stults
subject Wire R3 into the seats: 4a and 4b now judge derivations, not just items
STEP_stage4.md section 5.1 specifies 4a's denominator as "the rendered set
(R1+R2+R3)". readback_r3 was built but nothing consumed it, so the seats judged
items and rules and never WHY A VERDICT FOLLOWED. The design answers the
question the R3 build flagged as open -- a derivation is a 4a/4b item, not a
fifth denominator -- so this is implementation, not a decision.

R3 arrives as an optional argument rather than off the readback, because it
needs a stage-3 covering set and a solver run that plain rendering does not. A
caller without one gets R1+R2 and the denominator SAYS SO under
`r3-not-supplied`, so "no stage-3 result was given" can never read as "this
module has no derivations". A test pins that those two states are
distinguishable -- it is the vacuous-pass shape, and here the two would look
identical.

A situation deriving no verdict atom is excluded BY NAME as `no-derivation`,
never dropped: 8 of 18 covering-set situations across the stored modules derive
a verdict, so silently dropping the other 10 would overstate 4a's coverage by
more than a third.

4b filters 4a's output rather than re-deriving the set, so the two cannot drift.

RED-verified by mutation. 673 passed, 1 xfailed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit b50092ba91b63db1c66604f310e9966bb226953e
ordinal 109
date 2026-08-08 00:57:57 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Adversarial review of stage 4: 14 findings, 3 high
Clean-context review of the four review seats (29e018c), the R3 derivation
layer, and the R3->seats wiring (beb8531). REVIEW ONLY -- no code, test or
design document was changed. No API call, no spend.

The three highs are one shape, and it is this repo's named signature failure --
a check that cannot run, exiting like a check that passed:

* divergences() can NEVER fire. Each seat's closed verdict set is disjoint from
  every other's and every CONTRADICTION pair sits inside one seat's vocabulary,
  so 0 records over all 81 legal verdict combinations. All five tests that pin
  section 6 construct judgements validate_judgements refuses.
* The R3 wiring is a no-op against the real readback_r3.ModuleR3 -- it has
  `situations`, not `derivations`, and Derivation has no .item/.nodes. A module
  WITH a rendered derivation yields a 4a denominator identical to r3=None, and
  excluded=None, i.e. without even the r3-not-supplied marker. The guarantee is
  inverted. The tests pin a _D/_R3 duck type nothing in the repo builds, and
  plan_clause has no r3 parameter at all.
* mutate_seats.py reports "83 mutants applied, 0 survivor(s)", exit 0, against a
  RED test suite. No baseline check, no return-code triage, no collected-count
  comparison -- all three of which mutate_schema.py guards explicitly. The
  documented pyc trap IS fixed; a larger hole of the same class sits behind it.

Also confirmed: no join-key guard on the stage-3 discrimination cross-check (a
mismatched key makes every `covered` `unsupported` while the report says the
number was available); report_line is NOT byte-identical under a flipped 4a
verdict because the pooled unclear rate includes 4a; 4c is anchored against
readback.py and not against a rendering bug (dropping a rule body from
_item_text survives all 137 tests); refuse_aggregate scans top-level key names
only; RB4's non-evidential stamp cannot fire on the corpus (level 0.90, max
measured echo 0.74); a `%!` in a model-authored gloss is silently rewritten by
xclingo's own preprocessor -- the third Invariant-1 escape of the shape the
build already fixed twice.

Two directions where the CODE is right and the DESIGN is stale: section 7's
corpus-scale cost is falsified by seats.py --cost by an order of magnitude
($303 frontier worst, not ~$25 -- 35x the whole cap), and section 8's
registration requirement names fencing that exists only in
semi-formal-experiment/.

20 hand-written mutants, 6 survivors. The shipped sweep was re-run (83/0, real
but not trustworthy). R3's block-on-empty machinery and the seat-origin leak
fence were attacked and held.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 5201e52879b5cdceb237dce5a8a3cbaee17857cb
ordinal 110
date 2026-08-08 01:01:22 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject My R3 wiring was a NO-OP against every real object, and my tests pinned a fiction
Stage-4 review finding 2, HIGH, and it is mine. denominator_4a read
r3.derivations / d.item / d.nodes. readback_r3 builds NONE of those: ModuleR3
carries `situations`, a SituationR3 carries `derivations`, a Derivation is
(label, verdict, roots).

So the wiring never fired on anything the repo constructs -- and it failed in
the SILENT direction. A module WITH real derivations produced ids identical to
r3=None, and returned excluded=None, so the only state carrying a marker was
the honest-absence one while the silently-dropped one carried nothing. Exactly
backwards.

WORSE: all three tests passed, because they hand-wrote a duck type nothing in
the repo builds. One of them was named "the vacuous-pass shape". A fixture that
models the type wrongly tests the fixture -- which is the failure this
repository names as its signature, committed by the person quoting it.

Fixed against the real shape and verified on real objects: m0014 contributes
derivation S0 to 4a; m0037 derives nothing and is excluded by name as
no-derivation rather than vanishing. A new test asserts ModuleR3 and
SituationR3 still carry the fields the denominator reads -- including that
ModuleR3 does NOT carry `derivations`, so the original wrong wiring cannot
start working by accident and leave the comment lying. excluded is always a
dict now; it was None, and the membership tests would have raised TypeError.

676 passed, 1 xfailed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 0ecb617d74b4cc873612ac1f65427bdbf73a17ce
ordinal 111
date 2026-08-08 01:02:14 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Q-19: section 6 divergence can never fire, and the design is why
0 divergence records over all 81 legal verdict combinations. Every seat's
vocabulary is disjoint and every CONTRADICTIONS pair sits inside ONE seat. The
code implements the design literally: section 6 says "two seats reach opposite
verdicts" and its own worked example is faithful vs unfaithful, both 4b's.

This matters more than its size suggests. Section 4.3's guard is that unanimity
must not read as confirmation, and section 6 is the mechanism that makes
disagreement visible. If it cannot fire, four agreeing seats are the only
possible outcome -- the failure section 4 exists to prevent.

Three readings offered, none chosen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----
